account:
Today there seems to be an effort to arrange grain and bread supplies through trade or credit, though I do not yet know the full arrangement. At the mill inspection I found eighty hay bales in the stall, priced at two emeralds each, so grain was available there. Neighbour told me builder and freight wanted nineteen bales and were offering thirty-two oak planks plus agreed services. Neighbour also said innkeeper urgently needed grain and had mentioned credit or trade. This suggests difficulty paying rather than a simple absence of stock. At 11:26 I saw builder give oak planks to baker, which may be connected to those negotiations, but I did not see the terms or any grain exchanged.

Residents have repeatedly mentioned a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery, naming baker, innkeeper and sometimes freight as present. Nobody has explained what actually changed. Neighbour had heard only the same vague report and advised against treating it as confirmed. I cannot yet conclude that any bridge or ferry arrangement has changed. There are also reports of innkeeper carrying bread from the bakery and baker carrying bread near the inn, consistent with deliveries or redistribution, but their purpose has not been established firsthand.

Separately, the town account inquiry remains unresolved. The treasury held 128 emeralds but no account records; secretary's written inquiry said the great hall contained no records identifying who holds the missing figures. I have no evidence linking that problem to the grain trading. I am home for the noon appointment and should next attend the office at thirteen for council letters, then neighbour's cottage tea at fifteen and the approved great hall lighting inspection with builder at eighteen.
